reason: The passage depicts multiple regular human characters exercising agency throughout: Moses actively chooses to investigate, kill the Egyptian, and flee; two Hebrew men are engaged in a fight showing mutual action; a Hebrew man responds to Moses with direct speech, challenging his authority ('Who made you a ruler and judge over us?'); and Pharaoh hears of the matter and actively pursues Moses. These are all mortal, non-divine figures making consequential choices and taking deliberate actions, not merely passive recipients of divine will.
